nodes.text: Buyer spends a weekend chasing one house through stalling, a 20K price cut, and standoff, then walks away vindicated.

evidence.text: So, I've been looking for a house for almost a year now. It's been way longer than I expected and the market has been weird, to say the least. There are a lot of houses that come to the market and stay for a loooooong time and there are some that are gone in usually 1-2 days.

Thursday 5pm: a new house comes on the market. Friday 1pm: We see the house. I like it. I'm going to put an offer at the asking price. I don't want to get into a bidding war; I'll make the offer as sweet as possible so that they accept it right away.

Saturday 5pm: N calls, they say they have another offer which they're going to consider in an hour. My offer is much better than the other offer; they want to encourage me to rewrite the offer. I drop the offer by 20K from the asking price and remove most of those sweet things. N strongly advises me against doing it. I do it anyways.

One week later: N says he thinks the house had an offer of 5K above asking price. Two weeks later: the house is sold for 10K below the asking price. N is going to buy me a coffee! Also the first one that I put an offer on is gone for waaaaay higher than the asking price.

Transaction debrief via Claude: Negotiation Duration 3 Days (Friday-Sunday), Final Outcome: Walked away. Key Takeaway: In negotiations, information, emotional control, and strategic flexibility are more valuable than immediate transactional success.
